summary: This section explains what happens to the old Company Law Board when the new Tribunal and Appellate Tribunal are set up. It dissolves the old board and decides the future roles, jobs, and funds for its members and staff. Some members and regular employees move to the new bodies, while others return to their original departments or leave without claiming extra compensation.
points: The Company Law Board is dissolved when the new Tribunal and Appellate Tribunal are constituted.
Qualified existing leaders of the old board can temporarily serve as leaders of the new Tribunal or Appellate Tribunal until the new ones are formed.
Regular employees of the old board become employees of the new Tribunal or Appellate Tribunal with the same pension, gratuity, and benefits.
Employees who came on deputation either join the new Tribunal or Appellate Tribunal if qualified, or return to their parent department otherwise.
Staff who transfer to the new bodies are not entitled to any retrenchment compensation under any law.
Existing employee welfare and provident funds are transferred to the new Tribunal or Appellate Tribunal.
example: Mr. Sharma was a regular employee working at the old Company Law Board under Meera Textiles Private Limited administration context of government staffing. When the new Tribunal was finally constituted, his job automatically transferred to the new Tribunal. He kept his usual rights regarding pension and gratuity just like before. Meanwhile, Mr. Verma, who was only on deputation to the old board and did not meet the new qualifications, was sent back to his parent government ministry. Both men had to accept these shifts without claiming any special compensation for the change.

terms.meaning: A special court or official body set up to handle specific legal disputes.
A temporary transfer of an employee from one organization or department to another.
A lump sum money payment given to an employee by an employer as a token of appreciation for service.
A permanent core group of trained people serving in a specific organization or government branch.

watch: Do not assume that all employees of the old board automatically keep their jobs in the new Tribunal; only those meeting specific rules and regular employment terms are transferred.
